top_comments.text:
Guys, make tallow yourself and save $8-18 per pound. It's so easy. Buy ribeye roasts with a nice fat cap. (I get mine from a local grocery for $9-$10 per lb.). When you cut it into steaks, remove the fat cap and save it in the freezer. (The remaining steaks have plenty of fat remaining.) Accumulate fat caps in the freezer till you need more tallow. 

When you run out of tallow, thaw and mince the fat caps. Personally, I cut them into 1" bits and hand-grind them, but you can just mince them with a knife. Put a quarter cup of water and the mince into a slow cooker and cook on low for at least 4 hours, stirring once per hour. I start it in the evening and cook it overnight, so I stir only 2-3 times before I go to bed and it still comes out great. 

When the fat is fully liquified (you'll have some cracklings and maybe a couple bits of meat in there, but most is liquid), pour it through a strainer. Some folks line a pasta strainer with cheesecloth; I just strain through a fine metal tea strainer. A coffee filter might even work, but I don't like using anything that might contain plastics. Pour into mason jars (you may need three or four, and I used to just save old pickle jars and lids and use them. Refrigerate to store; I find it keeps for months and better than butter or hard cheese. With only 3-4 fat caps, you'll render enough tallow to do all your cooking for at least a month and probably two or three. Tallow is awesome for cooking beef, lamb, eggs (especially scrambled), fish, or vegetables. 

You'll save a lot of money, become more self-sufficient, and learn a skill that you'll need in the next zombie apocalypse. Although Walmart does often carry cheaper tallow, the last time I priced plastic jars of tallow in my local WalMart it was $18 per pound!
